# Enforcement-Actions Schema Reference Audit — 2026-08-02

**Scope:** audit only. No schema change, no rename, no drop, no migration was performed in this task.
**Table:** `public.enforcement_actions`, 80 columns (live list read from `information_schema.columns`, ordinal order preserved below).
**Method:** whole-repo word-boundary search (`rg -w <column>`) over `supabase/functions/**`, `src/**`, `tests/**`, `scripts/**`, `supabase/migrations/**`, `library/**`. Hits in the auto-generated `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts` are counted separately and are **not** evidence of use.

---

## 1. Headline result

**There are no genuine zero-reference columns.** Four columns have no reference anywhere outside the migration that created them and the generated types file:

| column | only reference |
|---|---|
| `strat_url_wellformed` | `supabase/migrations/20260801210903_fc8276ec-1ec7-43e6-8c1c-351f622b7100.sql` |
| `strat_subject_usable` | same migration |
| `strat_date_parseable` | same migration |
| `stratified_at` | same migration |

These are the Item-352 stratification-sweep outputs; they were written by SQL in that sweep and are read today only by ad-hoc `psql` analysis, not by application code. Note the sibling column `strat_has_document` is **not** in this group — it is part of `GATE_COLUMNS` in `supabase/functions/_shared/enforcement/surface-gate.ts` and is therefore live on every customer surface. Any future deprecation discussion should treat the four above as *migration-only*, not as *safe to drop*: they are the only persisted record of the stratification pass.

Twelve further columns have a thin but real production footprint (≤4 edge/frontend hits) and are the next tier worth scrutiny, not deprecation:
`disposition_type_extraction_method`, `appeal_status_extraction_method`, `sector_extraction_method`, `instrument_class_extraction_method`, `regulatory_family`, `last_source_fetch_at`, `statutory_provisions_evidence`, `source_quality`, plus the four above.

### Live consumers of the table (32 files)

Edge: `get-enforcement-context`, `get-enforcement-archive`, `get-memo-eligible-with-freshness`, `verification-scan`, `verification-queue-drain`, `corpus-refetch-campaign`, `corpus-extract-candidates`, `repair-corpus-subjects`, `batch-fetch-primary-sources`, `discover-primary-source-url`, `fetch-and-extract-primary-source`, `enrich-enforcement`, `enrich-legacy-corpus`, `per-regulator-ingestion`, `ingest-gov-enforcement`, `ingest-cms-tracker`, `ingest-gdprhub`, `fetch-updates`, `generate-weekly-brief`, `generate-custom-brief`, `generate-horizon-intelligence`, `process-li-updates`, `track3-discovery-orchestrator`, `track3-extract-orchestrator`, `_shared/ltp/eu-authority/fetch.ts`.
Frontend: `src/pages/Enforcement.tsx`, `src/pages/EnforcementActionDetail.tsx` (**selects `*` — every one of the 80 columns is fetched to the browser on this route**), `src/pages/admin/VerificationScanAdmin.tsx`, `src/pages/admin/CorpusExtractionAdmin.tsx`, `src/components/enforcement/EnforcementStats.tsx`, `src/components/cppa/BreachPrecedentMap.tsx`, `src/hooks/useEnforcementSignals.ts`.

The `select("*")` at `src/pages/EnforcementActionDetail.tsx:73` is the single most important fact for a future deprecation decision: it means no column is "invisible" at the transport layer, even where only ~21 fields are rendered (see §4).

## 2. The four product schemas that were "not located"

| product | schema location | touches enforcement? | columns it exposes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **cppa-admt** | `supabase/functions/_shared/report-schemas/admt.ts` (exists — `ADMT_REPORT_SCHEMA`, applied at `run-admt-checker/index.ts:2638`) | **Yes.** Declares `enforcement_context` (L145), `enforcement_precedents` (L150), `enforcement_meta` (L151), with nested `ENFORCEMENT_CONTEXT_KEYS` (L182) and frontend read paths `enforcement_context.aggregate_exposure_note` / `penalty_per_violation_*` / `penalty_statutory_basis` (L233–236) | whatever `get-enforcement-context` returns in `results` (the `ENFORCEMENT_SELECT` set) |
| **dpa-generator** | `supabase/functions/_shared/report-schemas/dpa.ts` (exists — `DPA_REPORT_SCHEMA`, applied at `generate-dpa/index.ts:1621` and `:1742`) | **Yes.** `enforcement_precedents` (L33), `enforcement_meta` (L34) | `get-enforcement-context` call at `generate-dpa/index.ts:502`, `tool: "dpa-generator"`, `articles: ["gdpr:28","gdpr:32","gdpr:33"]`, limit 8 |
| **registration** | **No report-schema file exists and none is needed** — `run-registration-assessment/index.ts` never calls `serializeCustomerReport`. Its customer shape is the inline `persistPayload` / `result_summary` at `run-registration-assessment/index.ts:655–668`, persisted to `registration_assessments.result_summary`; the deliverable builder lives under `_shared/ltp/…` registration deliverables | **No.** Single textual match for "enforcement" in the whole function (`index.ts:261`) is the phrase "supervisory or enforcement authority" in a fallback sentence. It never queries `enforcement_actions` and never calls `get-enforcement-context` | none |
| **biometric-checker** | **No report-schema file** — `check-biometric-compliance/index.ts` also does not call `serializeCustomerReport`. Its customer shape is the inline `report_data` literal at `check-biometric-compliance/index.ts:2008–2035` | **Yes**, via `get-enforcement-context` at `index.ts:1466` (`tool: "biometric-checker"`, `biometric: true`, `data_categories: ["biometric"]`, limit 12) → surfaced as `report_data.enforcement_precedents` (`enforcement_context.slice(0,5)`) and `enforcement_meta` | full `ENFORCEMENT_SELECT` row objects are embedded verbatim in `enforcement_precedents` |

**Consequence for a deprecation decision:** registration is the only one of the ten products with zero enforcement coupling. biometric-checker is *more* exposed than the schema-file products, not less: because it has no whitelist serializer, the raw retrieved rows (all ~31 `ENFORCEMENT_SELECT` fields, including `provisions_normalized`, `enrichment_version`, `source_database` and the seven gate columns) are persisted into `report_data.enforcement_precedents` unfiltered.

## 3. CCPA-regime call sites

`get-enforcement-context/index.ts:47` defines `ccpa: { jurisdictions: ["California","US-CA"], lawPatterns: ["%ccpa%","%cpra%","%california consumer privacy%"] }`. `resolveTier` (L59) returns `{null,null}` for `ccpa`, so ccpa queries take the untiered path at L348/L371. Every invocation with CPPA-direct intent:

| call site | line | request | current reachability |
|---|---|---|---|
| `supabase/functions/run-cppa-cybersecurity/index.ts` | 346–359 | `tool:"CPPA", regime:"ccpa", jurisdictions:["California","United States","US-CA"], breach:true, limit:6` | **live** and reached; returns empty under CPPA-INCLUSION-GATE |
| `supabase/functions/generate-improvement-kit/index.ts` | 222–229 | `regime:"ccpa", jurisdictions:["California","US-CA","United States"], limit:3` | live; per-item, fail-open — items are silently omitted when no cited row returns, so the gate makes the enforcement line permanently absent rather than erroring |
| `supabase/functions/run-cppa-risk-assessment/index.ts` | 486–487 | `regime:"ccpa", jurisdictions:["California","US-CA","United States"], limit:8` | **legacy function, no longer routed** — Item 359 flipped all 12 invocation sites to `run-cppa-risk-assessment-v2`. Dead call site |
| `supabase/functions/_shared/ltp/eu-authority/fetch.ts:91` | — | direct `enforcement_actions` query (not via the context service) selecting `subject, regulator, jurisdiction, decision_date, law, violation, fine_eur, source_url` + `GATE_COLUMNS` | **live on the v2 cppa-risk path** — this is the EU/EEA persuasive-authority pool, deliberately *not* a ccpa query (`PRODUCT_GATES["cppa-risk"]` is EU/EEA/UK only) |

No other file passes `regime: "ccpa"`. There is no frontend call site with ccpa intent (`src/hooks/useGdprEnforcementSignals.ts` passes GDPR regimes only; `src/hooks/useEnforcementSignals.ts` queries the table directly with no regime concept and no CPPA filter).

## 4. Fetched-but-dropped gap report (informational)

`ENFORCEMENT_SELECT` (`get-enforcement-context/index.ts:96`) returns 31 fields per row: `id, regulator, jurisdiction, subject, sector, industry_sector, law, violation, key_compliance_failure, preventive_measures, decision_date, fine_eur_equivalent, fine_amount, fine_verified, source_url, precedent_significance, data_categories, violation_types, tool_relevance, breach_related, biometric_related, statutory_provisions, provisions_normalized, enrichment_version, source_database` + the 7 `GATE_COLUMNS`, plus the computed `authority_tier` / `tier_label`.

| product | render function | fields that reach the customer text | fetched but dropped |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Governance** (baseline, already known) | `run-governance-assessment/index.ts` `enforcementContextStr` | subject, regulator, jurisdiction, decision_date, fine, key_compliance_failure | `preventive_measures`, `authority_tier`, `tier_label`, `statutory_provisions`, `provisions_normalized`, `precedent_significance`, `violation_types`, `data_categories`, `sector`/`industry_sector`, `source_url`, `tool_relevance`, `source_database`, `enrichment_version` |
| **DPIA** | `run-dpia-framework/index.ts:1138–1148` | subject, regulator, jurisdiction, decision_date, fine (`fine_eur_equivalent`, suppressed when `fine_verified === false`), key_compliance_failure ∥ violation, **`preventive_measures`** ("— Preventive: …"), **`statutory_provisions`** ("— citing …") | `authority_tier`/`tier_label` (fetched, tier is computed for `regime:"gdpr"`, never printed), `precedent_significance`, `source_url`, `violation_types`, `data_categories`, `provisions_normalized`, `tool_relevance`, `sector`/`industry_sector`, `source_database`, `enrichment_version`. **DPIA is the best case: it is the only product that renders `preventive_measures`.** |
| **LIA** | `run-li-assessment/index.ts:797–808` | subject, regulator, jurisdiction, decision_date, fine, key_compliance_failure ∥ violation, `statutory_provisions`, **`authority_tier` → rendered as the `TIER 1/2/3` tag** (`tierTagFor`, L787) | **`preventive_measures` — fetched, never printed** (the remediation content is the biggest single loss here, since LIA's balancing test is exactly where "what the regulator expected instead" would carry weight), `precedent_significance`, `source_url`, `violation_types`, `data_categories`, `provisions_normalized`, `tool_relevance`, `sector`/`industry_sector`, `source_database`, `enrichment_version`. `tier_label` is dropped in favour of the locally-derived tag string. |
| **IR-Playbook** | `generate-ir-playbook/index.ts` `formatEnforcementContext` (L504–520), injected at L907 | regulator, decision_date (twice: year for the citation, ISO for "decided"), `source_url`, fine (currency-switched £/€ on regulator/jurisdiction), `fine_verified` | **`preventive_measures` — dropped** (for a breach-response product this is the most directly actionable field in the row), **`key_compliance_failure` — dropped**, `subject` is not printed in the citation line, `statutory_provisions`, `authority_tier`/`tier_label` (null anyway — no `regime` is passed at L728–733, so the tiering path never runs for IR), `precedent_significance`, `violation_types`, `data_categories`, `provisions_normalized`, `tool_relevance`, `sector`. Note IR also re-persists the raw rows at L1773 (`enforcement_precedents: enforcement_context.slice(0,5)`), so the dropped fields still ship inside the report JSON — they just never reach prose. |
| **CPPA-Cyber** | `run-cppa-cybersecurity/index.ts:371–377` | id, regulator, subject, decision_date, violation ∥ key_compliance_failure, fine (`fine_eur_equivalent`, `fine_verified`), `source_url` | **`preventive_measures` — dropped**, `jurisdiction` — dropped, `statutory_provisions`, `authority_tier`/`tier_label` (null — `regime:"ccpa"` returns no tier), `precedent_significance`, `violation_types`, `data_categories`, `provisions_normalized`, `tool_relevance`, `sector`/`industry_sector`. In practice the whole block is empty today: `regime:"ccpa"` + CPPA-INCLUSION-GATE ⇒ zero rows. |
| **Biometric-checker** | no formatter — raw rows go into the prompt/report | (all, unfiltered, via `enforcement_precedents`) | none dropped; the opposite problem — no whitelist |
| **DPA-generator** | `generate-dpa/index.ts` | `enforcement_precedents` persisted through `DPA_REPORT_SCHEMA`; no prose formatter comparable to the above | tier fields null (no `regime` passed) |

**Cross-cutting observations (no action taken):**
1. `preventive_measures` is fetched for every product and rendered by exactly one (DPIA). It is the only field in the select list that carries remediation content.
2. `authority_tier`/`tier_label` are computed on every gdpr/uk_gdpr request but only LIA surfaces them, and only via its own re-derived label string. DPIA requests them (it passes `regime`) and discards them. IR, CPPA-Cyber and DPA never pass `regime`, so the tiering code runs and returns nulls — the binding-strength signal is unavailable to them by construction, not by choice.
3. `precedent_significance`, `provisions_normalized`, `tool_relevance`, `enrichment_version` and `source_database` are selected by all five products and rendered by none. `provisions_normalized` is used as a *filter* (`applyContentFilters`, L112), so it earns its place in the query but not in the projection.

## 6. What this audit does NOT establish

- It does not clear any column for removal. The only columns with no application-code reference at all are the four `strat_*`/`stratified_at` stratification outputs, and those hold the only persisted record of the Item-352 sweep.
- Because `src/pages/EnforcementActionDetail.tsx:73` selects `*`, every column is transported to the browser on that route regardless of whether it is rendered. Any drop decision has to be made against the rendered set (§4 / §5 "rendered /enforcement detail" flag), not against the transported set.
- No code, schema, migration, gate or surface was changed by this task.
